segments.text: Azure Migrate explains how applications move to Azure. AI Feasibility Assessment answers the next question: where can AI create value, and what evidence, controls, and proof are needed?

In the simulator, we select B P T co as a complete discovered application and choose Document Processing and Enrichment. The assessment reuses observed dependencies, runtimes, assessed targets, readiness, and cost without assuming AI is feasible.

The customer supplies what discovery cannot know: classify documents, extract fields, enrich metadata, validate rules, and route exceptions to people, targeting less manual work, faster processing, controlled access, and measurable accuracy.

After consent, Foundry improves only the grounded narrative; deterministic rules control eligibility, gaps, cost, and disposition. The versioned pack separates business, data, integration, governance, operations, and economics; proposes Document Intelligence, AI Search, model access, orchestration, storage, and monitoring; shows low, base, and high scenarios; and defines a bounded proof of concept with acceptance tests and production gates. Proof-of-concept candidate means justified experimentation, not production readiness.

One action opens linked AI-ready architecture. The base migration design remains intact, while proposed AI services appear as an explicit extension tied to the assessment revision and costed separately.

This converts migration context into an inspectable investment decision and delivery handoff. It may recommend a proof of concept, remediation, conventional automation, an existing product, or no AI. Azure Migrate understands the application; AI Feasibility helps choose its next value.
